old_problem: The historical review treated the Partial Add assembly state machine as target-specific and unresolved. IPMI 2.0 section 33.14 defines reservation/modal behavior, first request RID 0000h and offset 0, returned RID anchoring continuations, strictly sequential offsets, in-progress 0 versus final 1, reserved bits, pre-final discard and optional 80h length error. The Project still must supply one approved record, fixed split and safe recovery, but those are bounded configuration rather than missing command semantics. No generic SDR-record checksum may be invented.
disposition_reason: Split one absent owner-approved disposable SDR into at least two frozen fragments. Through the verified OOB endpoint, start 25h with the non-modal reservation, RID 0000h, offset 0 and in-progress 0; retain the returned RID for every continuation, advance each offset by exact prior data length, keep reserved bits zero, and mark only the last fragment 01h. Use reservation 0000h only inside explicitly supported modal update mode with an authoritative abort/Exit contract. Stop on any completion, RID, offset or session ambiguity without replay. After final commit, obtain fresh reservations for full 23h reconstruction and exact-key 26h deletion, then reconcile canonical repository and monitoring state. Pre-final non-modal failure is discarded by invalidating the reservation once; ambiguous final is searched by unique key before recovery. Never use ordinary Add/IB, clear/reset or automatic restart.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1211-1214, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests.json, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The corresponding IB Partial Add row 1085/new review event 226 and distinct OOB complete Add row 1211/event 235 were read. Formal queue sequence 86 was read from the locked queue and verified as row 1213 / variant 50ee37b87ce7ce86.

IPMI v2.0 Appendix G assigns Partial Add SDR to Storage NetFn 0Ah/Cmd 25h. Repository Info operation-support bit 2 advertises Partial Add, and a writable repository must support it when ordinary Add is absent.

Section 33.14 defines request bytes as Reservation ID LS/MS, continuation Record ID LS/MS, offset, in-progress field and fragment data. The first request uses RID 0000h and offset 00h; its successful response supplies the RID used for all continuations.

Fragments are sequential with no gaps or overlap. Intermediate requests use in-progress low nibble 0h, the final request 1h, and high-nibble reserved bits zero. A one-fragment transaction would not test continuation behavior and is rejected for this identity.

The record is not retrievable until final completion. Canceling the reservation before completion discards incomplete information; after failure, ED-38 requires recording the failure rather than starting a new attempt automatically.

Completion 80h can report final length inconsistent with the header Record-Length, but this controller check is optional. Independent validation always requires concatenated bytes exactly equal 5+Record-Length and complete post-commit readback.
Section 43 defines the five-byte Record ID/version/type/length header, key and body and no universal SDR checksum. OEM integrity bytes exist only under an authoritative OEM schema.

In modal update mode the request still carries reservation bytes but uses 0000h. Because the standard does not fully define an incomplete modal-assembly abort, modal execution is NOT READY without target authority for abort and Exit 2Bh recovery.

An ambiguous intermediate response cannot safely be replayed at the same offset. A pre-final non-modal sequence is discarded by invalidating its reservation once; a possibly committed final is enumerated once by stable unique key before any delete.

Final commit may invalidate reservations. Complete 23h readback and 26h deletion therefore use new reservations and revalidate stable key/body; final comparison ignores volatile RIDs and timestamps but not logical content.

OOB safety additionally binds DNS/IP to FRU/serial/firmware, protects credentials and preserves channel/session evidence. Local IB row 1085 and ordinary 24h Add cannot cross-credit this multi-request remote-path coverage.

ED-02 preserves identity; ED-03 protects OEM semantics; ED-13/ED-15 govern N/A and exact criteria; ED-17 preserves evidence; ED-19 separates IB/OOB; ED-28/ED-30 require recovery/approval; ED-34 parameterizes record/split; ED-38 prohibits retry.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Partial Add SDR (OOB Storage 0Ah/25h) reserved sequential assembly, final commit and exact cleanup
test_case.purpose: Exercise the OOB Partial Add transaction with at least two ordered fragments of one approved disposable record, prove endpoint, reservation, RID, offset and finalization behavior plus exact assembled readback, then remove only the committed record without ordinary Add, IB credit, broad clear or automatic restart.
required_package: Approved BMC/SUT/firmware and secret-safe LANPlus endpoint bound to FRU/serial, with writable repository, Partial Add and targeted Delete support, plus authoritative non-modal behavior or modal 0000h with explicit incomplete-transaction abort/Exit
Version-controlled APPROVED_SDR_BYTES with approved RID placeholder, valid version/type/Record-Length and unique key/body; registered IANA/owner schema for OEM bytes and no invented generic checksum

Frozen FRAGMENT_PLAN of at least two nonempty chunks concatenating exactly to the fixture, first offset 0, each next offset equal cumulative bytes, sizes within OOB transport limits and only the last in-progress value 01h
Immutable raw/decoded repository and monitoring baseline, capacity/allocation/mode proof, unique-key absence, inert or exact effect oracle, maintenance window and immediate confirmation
Pinned no-retry OOB per-fragment runner/evidence recorder; fresh-reservation 23h reader; exact-key 26h cleanup; reservation-cancel abort and vendor-approved modal recovery when applicable
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED STATEFUL OOB SDR PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind endpoint to BMC FRU/serial/firmware and keep credentials outside command arguments/logs. Export and canonicalize the repository by stable type/key/body; capture 20h info, 21h allocation when supported and authoritative mode; prove unique key absent, capacity sufficient and every fixture byte authoritative. Validate total=5+Record-Length, FRAGMENT_COUNT>=2, exact concatenation, first chunk includes header, offsets [0,cumulative lengths], OOB request fit and expected monitoring effect; do not invent a checksum. For non-modal obtain one 22h RESERVATION; for modal enter 2Ah once and use reservation 0000h only with approved abort/Exit recovery. Display endpoint, fragment hashes/offsets/flags and cleanup for immediate approval. Send fragment 0 once as 25h `[Rlo Rhi 00 00 00 00 DATA0]`; require completion 00h and valid RID. Send each non-final continuation once as `[Rlo Rhi RIDlo RIDhi OFFSET 00 DATAi]`; use `[Rlo Rhi RIDlo RIDhi OFFSET 01 DATAfinal]` only for the last. Require every completion 00h and identical RID; never read partial content, switch session or resend an offset. After final commit obtain a fresh reservation, reconstruct RID with bounded 23h reads, and require assigned RID in header plus exact equality of all remaining bytes and approved monitoring effect. Exit modal mode if entered. With another fresh reservation, revalidate stable key/body and issue one 26h delete for that RID; prove key absence and canonical count/capacity/overflow/content recovery. Keep 24h Add, 27h clear, initialization, reset and IB outside this coverage.
test_case.expected_result: Every authorized OOB 25h fragment completes 00h on the same bound session, returns one stable valid RID and follows the exact offset/flag plan; the record is invisible before final completion. The final fragment commits exactly one record, fresh-reservation 23h reconstruction matches all approved assembled bytes with the assigned RID, and only the approved contained monitoring footprint occurs. Exact-key 26h cleanup removes that RID and restores canonical repository/monitoring baseline with overflow clear while allowing volatile IDs/timestamps to differ. A pre-final non-modal reservation cancellation leaves the unique key absent. Any ambiguity, malformed sequence, visible partial record, unintended effect or incomplete cleanup is FAIL/NOT READY without restart.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact OOB identity and endpoint binding, authoritative 25h/mode/abort/Delete support, approved complete fixture, at least two exact fragments, one stable session/reservation/RID with correct offsets/flags, per-fragment completion, one final commit, complete 23h equality, expected monitoring behavior, targeted removal and canonical recovery. FAIL covers guessed fragments/OEM/checksum, one-fragment pseudo-test, gap/overlap/repeated offset, session or RID change, nonzero reserved bits, early 01h, final length mismatch, partial visibility, unintended monitoring effect, ordinary Add/IB substitution, secret exposure, clear/reset/restart or failed recovery. NOT READY covers absent fixture, capacity, split, mode/abort, unique key, Delete, containment or approval. N/A requires authoritative absence of Partial Add support; an OOB transport/session error is insufficient.
safety_gate: Use one absent owner-approved disposable record and frozen multi-fragment plan. Do not calculate new chunks while executing, alter the fixture or guess any standard/OEM byte.
Bind endpoint to asset/firmware and protect credentials. Keep one authenticated session where feasible; target/session ambiguity stops the sequence before another fragment.
Hold one reservation across the entire non-modal partial transaction; do not Reserve again until abort or post-final readback. In modal mode use 0000h only with explicit target abort/Exit authority.
Send every offset exactly once in order, high reserved bits zero, 01h only on the final fragment. Any ambiguous response stops; never replay or automatically restart from offset zero.
For pre-final non-modal failure, invalidate the reservation once and prove unique key absent. For an ambiguous final, enumerate once by stable key because commit may have occurred.
After commit obtain fresh reservations and recheck stable key/body immediately before exact deletion. Reconcile content logically because other RIDs may change.
Never clear SDR/logs, invoke ordinary Add/initialization/reset, switch to IB or conceal an incomplete state. If modal exit or cleanup is uncertain, preserve every fragment and escalate.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; BMC/SUT/firmware/FRU and OOB endpoint/channel binding; official 25h state-machine authority; distinct OOB ordinary Add and IB Partial Add identities
Immutable repository baseline/canonical multiset, capacity/allocation/mode and reservation or modal-abort authority, unique-key absence and monitoring baseline
Fixture source/hash and decoded header/key/body, Record-Length calculation, OEM owner if applicable, frozen fragment table with offset/length/in-progress/hash and immediate confirmation
Per-fragment exact redacted request, session identity, timestamp, completion and returned RID proving one sequence and no replay
Fresh-reservation complete 23h reconstruction, exact assembled comparison, repository metadata and monitoring/alert/control effect

Pre-final abort evidence or exact-key 26h cleanup after commit, final canonical repository/monitoring reconciliation and PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A; explicit statement that the review agent executed no DUT command
test_case.recovery: For a definitely pre-final failed or ambiguous non-modal request, do not continue or replay: obtain one new reservation to invalidate/discard incomplete state, verify the unique key absent and preserve every fragment response. A modal transaction requires preapproved firmware-specific abort plus one Exit 2Bh; without that contract do not start. If the final response is ambiguous, exit mode if applicable and enumerate once by stable key. Zero matches means no delete; exactly one match is deleted once after fresh reservation and key/body check; multiple or mismatched records escalate. Never restart automatically, clear/repopulate, reset, switch transport or guess a continuation.

source_conflict.reason: IPMI 2.0 section 33.14 resolves reservation, initial/continuation RID, offset, sequencing, finalization, pre-final discard and response semantics. The Review layer supplies the approved record/fixed split and removes log clearing/checksum guessing.

blocked.reason: The core multi-fragment state machine and non-modal abort are standard. Fixture, split plan, endpoint, capacity, effect oracle and mode-specific recovery are bounded Project prerequisites; modal targets without abort authority remain NOT READY rather than Pending.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact BMC/SUT/firmware/OOB endpoint; Partial Add/Delete and mode support; complete approved record; frozen multi-fragment offsets/flags; capacity/OOB limits; unique key/effect oracle; reservation-cancel or modal abort/Exit recovery; monitoring window and immediate approval.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER OOB MULTIFRAGMENT STATE-MACHINE DEFINITION ONLY; NO 25H/22H/23H/26H/2AH/2BH COMMAND, SDR/SEL CLEAR, INITIALIZATION, RESET, POWER OR OTHER DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Sections 33.2, 33.7 and 33.11-33.15 plus section 43 and Appendix G define Storage 0Ah/Cmd25h, reservation/modal behavior, initial and continuation RID, exact offset/in-progress state machine, discard before completion, optional final-length error, complete 23h readback and 26h cleanup.

project_authority: The SDR/BMC owner binds endpoint, repository mode/abort semantics, exact compatible fixture and OEM authority, frozen fragment plan, capacity/OOB limits, monitoring effect, confirmation and targeted cleanup. It cannot replace 25h with 24h/IB, invent checksum or chunk semantics, accept one fragment, replay ambiguity, ignore stable-key checks, expose secrets or recover by clear/reset/restart.
